subject: Linguistics
title: Coarticulation
description: A short lesson to help you apply Coarticulation.

hook.text: The 'k' in 'key' and the 'k' in 'car' are physically different sounds—but you hear them as identical.

buildup.text: Coarticulation means each sound is shaped by its neighbors—your mouth prepares for upcoming sounds.

discovery.text: There are no clear boundaries between sounds in speech—the signal is continuous, not segmented.

twist.text: This means speech recognition requires context: the 'same' sound looks different every time.

climax.text: Listeners use coarticulation as a cue—a lip rounding on 's' tells you a rounded vowel is coming.

punchline.text: Every sound carries a trailer for the next one.

quiz.question: What is coarticulation?
options: Sounds being shaped by neighboring sounds
